title: iframe title, sandbox, allow, referrerpolicy
learningObjectives: Explain iframe title, sandbox, allow, referrerpolicy and choose appropriate document or embedded-resource metadata.

understand.concept: An iframe embeds another browsing context. title provides an accessible name; sandbox restricts capabilities; allow controls permitted features through Permissions Policy integration; and referrerpolicy controls referrer information sent with the request. Use the least privilege needed.
understand.whyItMatters: Embedded content can introduce privacy, security, accessibility, and performance concerns. Do not grant broad sandbox permissions without understanding their effect, and avoid embedding untrusted content with unnecessary capabilities.
understand.analogy: An iframe is a window into another document; its title names the window and sandbox limits what the embedded page can do.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; metadata and embedding behaviour follow browser, HTTP, and search-engine processing rules.

explain.narrative: The iframe has an accessible title, a restrictive sandbox example, a referrer policy, and lazy loading. Real deployments must choose permissions according to the embedded service.

examples.code: <iframe title='Example documentation' src='https://example.com' sandbox='allow-scripts' referrerpolicy='no-referrer' loading='lazy'></iframe>
examples.explanation: The iframe has an accessible title, a restrictive sandbox example, a referrer policy, and lazy loading. Real deployments must choose permissions according to the embedded service.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered or document-head example demonstrating the HTML feature.

practise.guidedTask: Create an iframe embed with a useful title and restrictive sandbox. Document why each permission is required before adding it.
practise.independentTask: Prepare a document head or embed example. Check accessibility, security permissions, and whether metadata accurately describes the content.
hints: Use absolute canonical URLs when declaring a canonical target.
Never treat crawler directives as access control.
Use restrictive iframe permissions and a meaningful title.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>iframe title, sandbox, allow, referrerpolicy</title></head><body>
<iframe title='Example documentation' src='https://example.com' sandbox='allow-scripts' referrerpolicy='no-referrer' loading='lazy'></iframe>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the iframe title attribute?
options: To provide an accessible name for the embedded browsing context
questions.answer: To provide an accessible name for the embedded browsing context
questions.explanation: The title helps users of assistive technology identify the iframe's content.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide metadata and embedding?
options: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
Use metadata as a substitute for authentication
Grant every embedded document all permissions
questions.answer: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate and embedded resources should receive only necessary capabilities.
